questoes.pergunta: At a fintech, each dev on the team added the Jira MCP server with `claude mcp add --transport http jira https://mcp.jira.internal/mcp`. A new dev clones the repository, and their Claude Code doesn't see Jira. What is the BEST fix?
opcoes: Ask the new dev to copy the `~/.claude.json` of a colleague who already has Jira configured and working
Re-add it with `--scope project` (writes to the `.mcp.json` at the root) and commit the file
Put the server configuration in the project's `CLAUDE.md`
Add the server to `.claude/settings.local.json` and commit that file for the whole team
questoes.explicacao: Without `--scope`, the default is local (only that dev, in `~/.claude.json`). For the whole team, project scope = a versioned `.mcp.json`.
feedbacks: Copies someone else's personal settings (and possibly credentials); doesn't scale.
Correct.
CLAUDE.md holds instructions for the model, not server configuration.
That file isn't where MCP servers live and, by definition, it's personal (gitignored).

questoes.pergunta: A team added the entry `"observability": { "url": "https://mcp.obs.example.com/mcp" }` to `.mcp.json`. The server doesn't connect, and `/mcp` shows a startup failure. What should be fixed?
opcoes: Change the URL to `http://` instead of `https://`
Change the transport to SSE, which is the default for remote servers
Run Claude Code with `--debug` until the server connects
Declare `"type": "http"` in the entry
questoes.explicacao: An entry with `url` but no `type` is read as stdio and fails. A remote server always declares `type`.
feedbacks: Downgrading security doesn't fix the cause.
SSE is legacy and isn't the cause.
`--debug` helps diagnose; it doesn't fix anything.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A consulting firm wants to share, via git, the GitHub MCP server, which requires each dev's personal token. Which TWO practices meet this need? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: In `.mcp.json`, use `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}" }`
Commit a service user's token in `.mcp.json`, since the repository is private and only the team has access
Put `.mcp.json` in `.gitignore` and send the file by email
Each dev defines `GITHUB_TOKEN` in their own environment (or uses OAuth via `/mcp`)
Store the token in `CLAUDE.md` so the model passes it on to the server
questoes.explicacao: Secrets go in via `${VAR}` in the versioned file; the value comes from each dev's environment (or from OAuth).
feedbacks: Correct: the file can be shared without the secret.
A private repository isn't a vault; a literal secret under version control leaks.
Loses the sharing and spreads the file through a worse channel.
Correct: completes the variable expansion.
Exposes the secret to the model's context and to the repository.

questoes.pergunta: The productivity agent uses a database MCP server with the `run_query` tool. In the logs, before answering any question, it makes 15–20 calls trying to discover which tables and columns exist. What is the BEST improvement to the server?
opcoes: Increase the per-turn call limit
Paste the full database schema into the system prompt of every session, so the model already knows the tables
Expose the schema and the table catalog as resources that can be browsed and read
Create a `guess_table` tool that tries to guess the table name
questoes.explicacao: Resources are read-only, browsable content; a catalog reduces blind exploratory calls.
feedbacks: Allows more blind attempts instead of eliminating them.
Static and expensive: it spends context in every session, even when it isn't used.
Correct.
One more tool for guessing; the problem is the lack of a catalog.

questoes.pergunta: A dev wants to test, only in the current project, an experimental MCP server that only she will use, without affecting the team or her other projects. How should she add it?
opcoes: `claude mcp add` without `--scope` (local scope, the default)
`claude mcp add --scope project`
`claude mcp add --scope user`
Edit the project's `.mcp.json` and simply not commit that change
questoes.explicacao: Local is the default: only you, only this project, stored in `~/.claude.json`.
feedbacks: Correct.
Would write to the shared `.mcp.json`.
Would apply to all of her projects.
Fragile: the versioned file stays dirty, and the server ends up committed by accident.

questoes.pergunta: A dev uses a personal note-taking MCP server in every repository he works in and doesn't want to configure it repo by repo or expose it to his colleagues. Which scope?
opcoes: local
project
managed
user
questoes.explicacao: User = all your projects, in `~/.claude.json`, without sharing.
feedbacks: Local applies only to the current project.
Project shares with the team via git.
Managed is organization policy, set by the admin.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A dev read that MCP's 'local' scope is personal and put the server definition in `.claude/settings.local.json`. The server doesn't show up. What is the explanation?
opcoes: The file needs to be committed to the repository for Claude Code to start taking it into account
MCP's local scope lives in `~/.claude.json`, not in `settings.local.json`
Servers defined as local only work with the SSE transport, which must be declared in `type`
The server still needs to be approved with `/mcp`, since every new server needs approval before it shows up
questoes.explicacao: A classic trick: MCP's local scope ≠ `.claude/settings.local.json`.
feedbacks: A local file is precisely what you don't commit, and it isn't where servers live.
Correct.
Scope and transport are independent.
There's nothing to approve: the server wasn't even read from that file.

questoes.pergunta: A company's internal MCP server requires an SSO token that expires every 60 minutes. Today the devs paste the token into `headers` and, every hour, the server stops responding. What is the BEST solution?
opcoes: Ask the security team for long-lived, non-expiring tokens specific to the MCP server
Switch the transport to stdio
Use `headersHelper` with a command that obtains a fresh token each time the headers are generated
Restart Claude Code every hour
questoes.explicacao: `headersHelper` generates the headers dynamically: it's the mechanism for short-lived credentials.
feedbacks: Weakens security to work around a configuration problem.
The server is remote; changing the transport doesn't apply.
Correct.
A manual stopgap that doesn't solve anything.

questoes.pergunta: A dev clones an open-source repository whose `.mcp.json` declares a stdio server that runs `node scripts/server.js`. Which TWO statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: The server runs automatically as soon as Claude Code opens, without asking anything
Servers coming from `.mcp.json` (project scope) ask for approval in the interactive session before running
To speed up onboarding, the recommendation is to pre-approve all project servers on every machine on the team
The server is ignored because `.mcp.json` only accepts remote servers
The approval exists because the file can start an arbitrary process; review the command first
questoes.explicacao: Project servers ask for approval: a repository can't run processes on your machine without consent.
feedbacks: Exactly what the approval prevents.
Correct.
Removes the protection against untrusted repositories.
`.mcp.json` accepts both stdio (`command`/`args`/`env`) and remote servers.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A .NET dev wrote a stdio MCP server with the `ModelContextProtocol` SDK. The server connects and drops right afterward, with a parse error on the client. The code uses `Console.WriteLine` to log each request. What is the likely cause?
opcoes: In stdio, stdout is the JSON-RPC channel; logs need to go to stderr
The C# SDK only supports Streamable HTTP
`"type": "stdio"` wasn't declared in `.mcp.json`
The server needs to implement the sampling primitive to be accepted by Claude Code
questoes.explicacao: With the stdio transport, any text on stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC messages; log to stderr.
feedbacks: Correct.
The SDK supports stdio (`WithStdioServerTransport`).
With `command`, stdio is implicit; that doesn't explain the parse error.
Sampling is optional, and it's a client primitive.

questoes.pergunta: A SaaS company publishes a remote MCP server that authenticates users with OAuth 2.0. How should devs configure it in Claude Code?
opcoes: As stdio, passing the manually obtained OAuth token in the `env` variable
As SSE, which is the remote transport that supports the OAuth flow in Claude Code
With `headers` containing the dev's username and password encoded in base64
As Streamable HTTP (`"type": "http"`), authenticating via `/mcp` in the session
questoes.explicacao: Streamable HTTP is the remote transport with OAuth; login is done via `/mcp`, and Claude Code stores and refreshes the token.
feedbacks: The server is remote; stdio is a local process.
SSE is legacy; OAuth is in Streamable HTTP.
A literal credential, and without the OAuth flow the server requires.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A bank's security team wants to ensure that devs use only MCP servers approved by the company, without depending on each person configuring things correctly. Which mechanism?
opcoes: A `.mcp.json` in each company repository listing only the servers approved by security
A rule in the company's `CLAUDE.md` forbidding other servers
Managed configuration (organization policy) with the allowed/denied servers
User scope configured on each dev's machine
questoes.explicacao: Managed is the governance scope pushed by the admin; it applies regardless of what the dev configures.
feedbacks: Devs can still add local/user servers on the side.
A prompt is probabilistic; a security rule goes in configuration/code.
Correct.
Depends on each person and can be changed by the dev.

questoes.pergunta: An MCP server's `get_logs` tool returns ~60k tokens of raw logs; Claude Code shows a warning and truncates the output, and the agent loses the part with the error. What is the BEST architectural fix?
opcoes: Increase `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` to 100k, so the entire log fits without truncation
Have the server filter and paginate (level, time range, limit) and return only what's relevant
Ask the model to ignore the first lines of the log
Switch the transport to Streamable HTTP, which has no limit
questoes.explicacao: [the numbers are volatile] MCP output is subject to a warning and truncation. The architect's fix is for the server to return less, in a more useful form.
feedbacks: Helps in isolated cases, but floods the context and degrades the rest of the session.
Correct.
The text has already arrived truncated; the model can't recover what was cut.
The limit belongs to the host, not the transport.

questoes.pergunta: A documentation MCP server needs to generate a summary of a long document before returning it, but the company doesn't want the server to have its own LLM API key. Which primitive makes this possible?
opcoes: Sampling: the server requests a completion from the host's model
Elicitation: the server asks the user for the summary
Resources: the server publishes the entire document, and the model reads and summarizes it
Roots: the server requests access to the document's directory
questoes.explicacao: Sampling lets the server request completions from the host's model, without credentials of its own.
feedbacks: Correct.
Elicitation asks the user for input, not the model.
It would handle the reading, but it doesn't generate the summary inside the server.
Roots deals with access boundaries, not generation.

questoes.pergunta: An infrastructure MCP server has a `delete_environment` tool. Before deleting, it needs the user to type the environment's name to confirm, in the middle of execution. Which protocol primitive?
opcoes: Sampling
Server prompts
Roots
Elicitation
questoes.explicacao: Elicitation: the server asks the user for input/confirmation through the client during the operation.
feedbacks: Sampling requests a completion from the model, which can't confirm on the user's behalf.
Prompts are templates invoked by the user, not a confirmation in the middle of execution.
Roots defines URI/filesystem boundaries.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: In a support agent that consumes three MCP servers (orders, CRM, logistics) via the Agent SDK, which TWO statements about the architecture are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Before listing tools, each client sends `initialize`, negotiating version and capabilities
The model opens the connections to the three servers and sends `tools/call` directly to each of them
The host maintains three clients, one per server
A single client multiplexes the three servers, to save connections and simplify authentication
`tools/call` can be sent before `initialize` if the tool is already known
questoes.explicacao: A host with one client per server (1:1); each connection starts with the `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` handshake.
feedbacks: Correct.
The model emits `tool_use`; it's the host's client that speaks JSON-RPC with the server.
Correct.
The architecture is 1:1.
The handshake is mandatory before any operation.

questoes.pergunta: The SRE team wants to distribute, through its own incidents MCP server, a standardized investigation playbook that devs trigger whenever they want, like a command. Which primitive should they use?
opcoes: An `investigate_incident` tool that the model decides to call when it sees fit
A resource with the playbook in markdown
A server prompt, which becomes the slash command `/mcp__incidents__<name>`
Elicitation asking the dev to paste the playbook
questoes.explicacao: Prompts are reusable templates invoked by the user; in Claude Code they become slash commands.
feedbacks: A tool is chosen by the model; the requirement is explicit invocation by the user.
It would be read-only; it doesn't become an invocable command.
Correct.
Inverts the flow: the playbook should come from the server.

questoes.pergunta: A dev has a `docs` server defined in the project's `.mcp.json` pointing to production, and also a `docs` server in local scope pointing to a test server. Which one does Claude Code use in this project?
opcoes: The one in `.mcp.json`, because project always wins
The local-scope one, because local > project > user
Both, automatically renamed to `docs` and `docs-1`
Neither; duplicate names disable the server
questoes.explicacao: With identical names, the more specific scope wins: local > project > user.
feedbacks: Inverts the precedence.
Correct.
There is no automatic renaming.
Nothing gets disabled; precedence applies.

questoes.pergunta: A dev runs `claude mcp add spreadsheets npx -y @company/spreadsheets-mcp` and gets an unknown option error for `-y`. How should it be fixed?
opcoes: `claude mcp add spreadsheets -- npx -y @company/spreadsheets-mcp`
`claude mcp add --transport http spreadsheets npx -y @company/spreadsheets-mcp`
`claude mcp add --scope project spreadsheets npx -y @company/spreadsheets-mcp`
Remove `-y` and confirm the installation manually every time
questoes.explicacao: `--` separates `claude`'s options from the stdio server's command; without it, `-y` is read as a `claude` flag.
feedbacks: Correct.
It's a local stdio server; HTTP requires a URL.
Scope doesn't solve the flag parsing.
Works around the problem instead of fixing it, and breaks in non-interactive use.

questoes.pergunta: A dev connected 9 MCP servers to Claude Code and realizes that the tool definitions would take up a good part of the context. He is thinking about removing servers he uses only occasionally. What should he consider first?
opcoes: Remove the least-used servers, since that's the only way to save context in Claude Code
Merge the 9 servers into one so there's only a single client
Ask in CLAUDE.md for the model to ignore the tools from the rarely used servers
Rely on MCP tool search, which loads the definitions on demand
questoes.explicacao: [the details are volatile] In Claude Code, MCP tool search is on by default and avoids loading all the definitions up front.
feedbacks: Loses capability unnecessarily.
A lot of rework; and one client per server is the architecture, not the problem.
The definitions would still take up context; a prompt doesn't remove tools.
Correct.
